question:
Four days after undergoing a craniotomy and evacuation of a subdural hematoma, a 56-year-old man has severe pain and swelling of his right leg. He has chills and nausea. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, and was started on hemodialysis 2 years ago. Prior to admission, his medications were insulin, enalapril, atorvastatin, and sevelamer. His temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), pulse is 110/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Examination shows a swollen, warm, and erythematous right calf. Dorsiflexion of the right foot causes severe pain in the right calf. The peripheral pulses are palpated bilaterally. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Leukocyte count 11,800/mm3
Platelet count 230,000/mm3
Serum
Glucose 87 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in treatment?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with severe pain and swelling in right leg" -> "Signs of possible deep vein thrombosis (DVT) present" -> "DVT can lead to pulmonary embolism if untreated" -> "Unfractionated heparin is standard treatment for DVT" -> "Initiating anticoagulation reduces risk of complications" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has erythema and warmth in right calf" -> "Symptoms suggest inflammation or thrombosis" -> "Dorsiflexion pain indicates possible DVT" -> "DVT management typically involves anticoagulation" -> "Unfractionated heparin is effective for acute DVT" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of chronic kidney disease" -> "Kidney disease increases risk of thromboembolic events" -> "Acute symptoms suggest urgent intervention needed" -> "Unfractionated heparin is safe in renal impairment" -> "Immediate treatment is crucial to prevent complications" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient's vital signs show fever and tachycardia" -> "Infection or thrombosis could be the cause" -> "Swollen, painful leg raises suspicion for DVT" -> "Unfractionated heparin is the first-line treatment" -> "Prompt treatment is necessary to avoid serious outcomes" -> 88%
analysis: The patient presents with signs and symptoms suggestive of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the context of recent surgery and risk factors including diabetes and chronic kidney disease. The warm, swollen, and erythematous right calf, along with pain on dorsiflexion (Homan's sign), supports this diagnosis. The most appropriate next step in treatment for DVT is the initiation of anticoagulation therapy. Unfractionated heparin is commonly used in acute settings, especially in patients with renal impairment, as it can be monitored and adjusted accordingly. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in treatment is unfractionated heparin therapy.
